title: Long-Term Hardship Hold Income Records: Counting Point by Nearness of the Next Review
content:
**Decision table — Hardship and Protective Holds.** For updated household income records asked for before a status review of a running Long-Term Hardship Hold, the point the income records due date is counted from depends on how soon the status review that next falls due will fall due, counted in calendar days from the day of the request. Reviews of this tier fall due every 60 calendar days counted from the hold's start date. A status review falling due on the day of the request counts as already fallen due, so the review that next falls due is the following one.

| The next review falls due | The income records are due |
|---|---|
| Within the short-notice days of the request — 7 calendar days or fewer after it | The tier's documentation days, 21 calendar days, after the request |
| Later than 7 days but no later than the tier's review overdue days, 15 calendar days, after the request | 21 calendar days after the review's due date |
| Otherwise — more than 15 days after the request | On the last day of the review's overdue window, 15 calendar days after the review's due date |

The days allowed for the income records are the calendar days from the day of the request to the due date so found, a whole number.

## Rows on both sides of each threshold

| Days from the request to the next review | Due date | Days allowed |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | 21 days after the request | 21 |
| 7 | 21 days after the request | 21 |
| 8 | 21 days after the review's due date | 29 |
| 15 | 21 days after the review's due date | 36 |
| 16 | 15 days after the review's due date | 31 |
| 40 | 15 days after the review's due date | 55 |

## Example (hypothetical)

A hold started on 1 March; reviews fall due on 30 April, 29 June and 28 August. A request made on 20 June finds the next review 9 days away — later than 7 days and no later than 15 — so the income records are due 21 days after 29 June, on 20 July: 30 days allowed.
